_national.labelling: PDO (POP, formerly OPAP for dry wines and OPE for sweet wines) and PGI (PGE, formerly Topikos Oinos). Traditional terms for PDO wines include Reserve (Epilegmenos) and Grande Reserve (Eidika Epilegmenos), whose ageing rules are set in each specification; Verdea (Zakynthos) and Retsina are protected traditional appellations under PGI.

gr-santorini.varieties: Dry white: at least 85% Assyrtiko, balance Athiri and Aidani. Vinsanto and liqueur wine: at least 51% Assyrtiko, balance Aidani, Athiri and small amounts of Gaidouria, Katsano, white Muscat, Monemvasia, Platani, Potamisi, Roditis.
gr-santorini.min_alcohol: Dry white: at least 12% natural and actual. Vinsanto: grapes at least 15% potential (260 g/l) before sun-drying and 21% (370 g/l) after; at least 21% total and 9% actual. Liqueur wine: at least 21% total, 15 to 22% actual.
gr-santorini.ageing: Dry white Reserve (Epilegmenos): at least 1 year incl. 6 months oak and 3 months bottle; Grande Reserve (Eidika Epilegmenos): at least 2 years incl. 12 months oak and 6 months bottle. Vinsanto and liqueur wine: at least 24 months oxidative ageing in oak, which must take place on Thira or Therasia.
gr-santorini.styles: Dry white; naturally sweet white from sun-dried grapes (Vinsanto: grapes dried in the sun, typically 7 to 12 days; no added concentrate, alcohol or distillate); liqueur wine from sun-dried grapes (fortification added by 31 May of the following year). Nykteri: dry PDO Santorini traditionally at least 13.5% with at least 3 months in oak (per Wines of Greece; not in the single document).
gr-santorini.labelling: Vinsanto may carry the harvest year ("Esodeia") after the 2-year minimum, or an age statement of 4, 8, 12, 16 years (four-year steps). Every lot passes an official tasting panel. Dry white fermented at max 20 C. Vines trained as traditional baskets (kouloura) or linear forms; zone is Thira and Therasia.
